# Rendered QA report (Deliverable E): HOLD (QA-F1 fixed; others open)

**Date:** 2026-11-01. **Build under test:** the private previews generated by `tools/build.py` from R48 `dbd53411`. **This is not a QA pass of the live site.** Nothing was published, no WordPress page was touched, and no QD PASS or accessibility certification is claimed.

## Scope and honest limits
- **Tested:** 45 locally built preview pages (35 articles, the water planner, 8 section hubs, the landing page) at **360, 390, 768, 1440 and 1920 px** (225 page-width combinations) in Microsoft Edge (Chromium) via Playwright on Windows 11. Axe-core 4.9.1 at 390 and 1440 px on all 45 pages (90 runs).
- **NOT tested:** how the **live Assembler theme** renders any of this (a second page-title H1, content-width clamp, whether inline `<style>`/`<script>` survive output, theme font loading); real phones or tablets; Safari or Firefox; any screen reader (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver); 200% zoom and large-text modes; forced-colors appearance; Lighthouse or Core Web Vitals on a hosted server (local-file load times below are **not** CWV); human visual review of every page. I looked at 3 screenshots myself; 12 are saved for a human to review.
- Everything below is automated measurement plus limited visual inspection.

## QA-F1 fix (applied after the first pass; shared `tools/build.py` and `assets/preparedness.css`)
**Change (narrow containers, under 900 px wide, only):**
- The table of contents is a collapsed `<details>` ("On this page (11 sections)"; 44 px tap target). In wide containers a 3-line inline script opens it, so desktop looks as before. With JavaScript off it stays collapsed on desktop too (still one click, fully usable).
- The breadcrumb shows only its parent link ("< Water"); the section/track chips (they repeat the kicker above the title) and the topic-tag chips are hidden. The status chips (Draft, Safety review pending) always stay.
- The "Print this guide" button moves from the header to the end of the article on narrow screens (both versions are hidden when printing).
- Header spacing is tightened. Wide layouts keep the original header, chips and button; their only change is that the table of contents now has a summary line instead of a heading.

**Measured result** (35 articles, local previews in Edge, `RENDERED-QA-F1-AFTER-2026-11-01.json`):

| Viewport | Action box top, before (median / max) | After (median / max) | Starts on first screen, before | After |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 390x844 | 1,151 / 1,347 px | **593 / 653 px** | 0 of 35 | **35 of 35** |
| 360x740 | 1,215 / 1,422 px | **610 / 680 px** | 0 of 35 | **35 of 35** (26 of 35 fully above 85% of screen height) |

The water planner page (the 36th page; not in the table's 35 articles) now has its action box at 529 px (390 wide) and 577 px (360 wide). Its tool form starts lower, at about 1,120 px, as before.

**Regression checks** (`RENDERED-QA-F1-REGRESSION-2026-11-01.json`): axe 0 violations in 90 runs (390 and 1440 px); no horizontal overflow at 390, 768 or 1440 px; no JavaScript errors; wide TOC open 35/35 with JS; narrow TOC closed 35/35; the summary is the third Tab stop and toggles with Enter; print hides the TOC and both print buttons while keeping the sources section (35/35); full native test run: 3,753 tests, 53 failures, all in the same four Windows categories as the R47 baseline (24 symlink privilege, 12 fixture newline, 5 export byte, 12 nondeterministic Errno 22 temp writes; the Errno 22 count varies from run to run), none involving markup or content. `validate.py`: 0 errors.

**Trade-offs and limits.** On phones the topic tags are no longer visible on article pages (they remain in hub cards and on wide layouts). Where JavaScript is off on desktop the TOC starts collapsed. The box now starts on the first screen, but at 360x740 only its first lines are visible, and a user on a short or large-text phone may still scroll. This was measured locally only: it has not been checked in the live Assembler theme (which may add its own title block above the content), on real devices, with a screen reader, or by a human reviewer.

## Files
`RENDERED-QA-LAYOUT-2026-11-01.json` (per page and width), `RENDERED-QA-DEEP-2026-11-01.json` (links, keyboard, no-JS, print, motion, axe, planner), `RENDERED-QA-ACTION-BOX-POSITION-2026-11-01.json`, 12 first-pass screenshots plus 4 `f1-after-*` screenshots in `qa-shots/`, and the scripts in `scripts/`.

## What must still happen before this can count as QA
A human visual review of all pages at phone and desktop sizes; a render check in the live theme on an authenticated draft preview; a real screen-reader and keyboard walkthrough; iOS Safari, Android Chrome and Firefox spot checks; hosted Lighthouse/CWV; and review of the QA-F1 change (it touches shared build and CSS) and a live-theme check that it still puts the box high on the page.
